events.name: FS_CREATE
events.description: A new file appears in the watched tree. This is how new media enters the index: the watcher debounces the notification and the file is submitted for indexing. Also fires for just a sidecar (.xmp) landing next to an existing asset.
effects: Row exists matching the file (path, decoded metadata), or the file is rejected with a logged skip reason and no row (undecodable/unsupported).
A create for just the .xmp of an existing asset results in the row augmented with sidecar metadata (resubmit sibling media path; mapping specified, not yet implemented).

faults.consequence: file undiscovered until the next scan
event logged, no row added (unprocessable paths are never indexed)
generation order decides; modeled in eventual-consistency.qnt

events.notes: Watcher-debounced create; the submit step is tracked separately as SUBMIT. Decode/scan failure: event logged, no row added (unprocessable paths are never indexed). A create for just the .xmp of an existing asset resubmits the sibling media path (never the xmp path itself, which fails the media-extension gate) so the row is augmented with sidecar metadata; covers delayed sidecar arrival via background transfer. The xmp-to-media mapping is specified, not yet implemented.

events.name: FS_MODIFY
events.description: An existing file's contents change on disk (same path, new bytes). The watcher debounces and resubmits the path; a snapshot mismatch (mtime+len) forces a full reprocess.
effects: Row converges to the new bytes' metadata; derived artifacts refreshed.

faults.consequence: row stays stale until the next scan

faults.fault: modify arrives while the same path is mid-processing
faults.consequence: in-flight item dropped; nothing resubmits it until the next watcher event or scan (healing owner open, S6)
settled state unchanged
event logged, prior row unchanged

events.notes: Watcher-debounced modify; the submit step is tracked separately as SUBMIT. See ASS-5. Same as create: decode failure is logged with no row added; an xmp-only modify resubmits the sibling media path for augmentation (specified, same mapping as create).

events.name: FS_MODIFY_INFLIGHT
events.description: Timing case, not a distinct external shape: the file changes while the pipeline is already processing that same path. Named separately because the outcome differs from a plain modify.
preconditions: item for same path being processed
effects: The in-flight item is dropped, never applied over newer state; the newer content is (re)processed.

faults.fault: no resubmit after the in-flight item is dropped
faults.consequence: path unchanged until the next watcher event or scan (healing owner open, S6)

events.notes: No dedicated in-flight modify hook verified; ForceModify models a concurrent edit during processing.

events.name: FS_DELETE
events.description: A watched file is removed from disk. Handled directly via the remove lane, not deferred to the sweep; ghosts cover missed events only.
effects: Row pruned (record kept, minus the path, only if other paths remain).
Thumbnail references decremented.

faults.consequence: ghost row until sweep marks sweepPending
generation order decides; stale remove superseded (modeled)

events.notes: Watcher-observed deletion prunes the row directly via the remove lane (record kept only if other paths remain, else the row is removed); ghosts and sweepPending cover missed events only. See ASS-3.

events.name: FS_RENAME_FILE
events.description: A single file is renamed or moved within the tree: same content, new path. Watchers report renames differently per platform, so the safe handling is specified as old-path remove plus new-path create, including a separately renamed sidecar.
effects: Row follows to the new path with no ghost window and no re-decode (specified: remove + create).

faults.fault: old path ghosts until sweep under current handling
faults.consequence: stale row visible briefly; converges at sweep

faults.fault: in-flight items for the old path
faults.consequence: superseded or fail-open; walkthrough not done

events.notes: Specified and modeled: treat as old-path remove plus new-path create, including a separately renamed sidecar (which resubmits its media path); converges with no ghost window. The model performs the explicit old-remove submit (ExternalRenameFile); the code still ghosts the old path until sweep - the gap is implementation-side.

events.name: FS_RENAME_DIR
events.description: A directory is renamed or moved: all contained assets move atomically with it, sidecar association follows by name.
effects: Every contained asset's row updated to the renamed path in one step, assetId preserved (ApiMove semantics, no intake); content-keyed derived artifacts untouched.

faults.fault: no watcher or code path exists (Modify arm drops non-file paths)
faults.consequence: contained files get neither remove nor index submits; rows under old path ghost, new paths undiscovered until scan/sweep
no generation bump on move (verified); absorbed by open-fail/skip - unproven

events.notes: Specified and modeled: a directory rename atomically renames all contained assets - direct row update preserving assetId and path per descendant (ExternalRenameDir / ApiAssignDirMove, SUBTREE_PAIRS at the finite bounds); sidecar association follows the renamed path by name; content-keyed derived artifacts require no moves. No verified watcher or code path (the Modify arm drops non-file paths, so contained files currently get neither remove nor index submits).

events.name: FS_ATOMIC_REPLACE
events.description: A file (main or sidecar) is replaced wholesale by an atomically written new file at the same path - editors and sync tools do this via temp-file plus rename.
effects: Handled as modify: media path resubmitted, snapshot mismatch forces full reprocess.
If the replace surfaces as rename events, rename handling applies; same-path collapse (remove then create) still converges.

faults.fault: replace surfaces as remove+create on one path
faults.consequence: delete first, then index fresh; converges

events.notes: Handled as modify in both cases (main file and sidecar): resubmit the media path; snapshot mismatch forces full reprocess (see ASS-5). If the replace surfaces as rename events rather than modify events, the rename handling applies instead; same-path rename-collapse (remove then create on one path) still converges: delete first, then index fresh.

events.name: FS_SIDECAR_CREATE
events.description: A sidecar (.xmp) newly appears next to an existing asset - for example a background transfer delivers it after the media file.
effects: Row augmented with sidecar metadata (sibling media path resubmitted; a present sidecar forces reprocess).

faults.consequence: resubmit open-fails; the media's own create event indexes it when it lands

faults.fault: xmp-to-media mapping unimplemented (watcher gate drops xmp events)
faults.consequence: xmp-only events dropped today; augmentation does not happen until a code change

events.notes: A create for just the .xmp of an existing asset resubmits the sibling media path (never the xmp path itself: sidecars fail the media-extension gate); reprocessing augments the row with sidecar metadata, since a present sidecar forces reprocess. Covers delayed sidecar arrival via background transfer; if the media file itself is not yet present, its own create event indexes it when it lands. Ordering: independent of the media event's arrival - generations supersede stale items and reprocessing is idempotent, so no cross-path coalescing is required for convergence (the 1s debounce stays per-path efficiency only). Specified; xmp-to-media mapping not yet implemented.

events.name: FS_SIDECAR_MODIFY
events.description: An existing sidecar's contents change on disk, for example when a metadata editor rewrites it.
effects: Row's sidecar-derived metadata refreshed via full reprocess (sibling media path resubmitted).

faults.consequence: same gap as FS_SIDECAR_CREATE

events.notes: Same handling as create: resubmit the sibling media path; full reprocess refreshes sidecar-derived metadata (including a separately renamed sidecar, handled as delete plus create converging to the same state). Ordering: as FS_SIDECAR_CREATE - independent resubmits converge regardless of order. Specified; same mapping as create.

events.name: FS_SIDECAR_DELETE
events.description: A sidecar (.xmp) next to an existing asset is removed; the row must drop the metadata derived from it.
effects: Row drops sidecar-derived state (sibling media path resubmitted; reprocess must drop it).

faults.fault: hash short-circuit (when enabled) cannot distinguish 'never had a sidecar' from 'sidecar deleted' (REQ-1)
faults.consequence: a bare resubmit would still skip; stale tags/descriptions/trashed flags persist indefinitely

events.notes: Resubmit the sibling media path; reprocessing must drop the sidecar-derived state. The model carries sidecar identity in the row and the submit snapshot (ExternalSidecarDelete), which forces reprocess and converges; the current code reprocesses and drops the stale state. The deferred hash short-circuit would need sidecar identity either in the submit snapshot (no schema change) or stored on the row (schema change), so a bare resubmit does not skip (REQ-1). See ASS-3.

events.name: API_UPLOAD
events.description: A client uploads a new asset over HTTP. The file is placed atomically (tmp written into the target dir, mtime set, then atomic rename to the final name) and the row is written synchronously; the intake queue is not involved.
effects: Row visible after the upload barrier (G3 queued: upload waits on the flush batch; assign and delete unverified).
Validation failure rejects with no row.

faults.consequence: reads may not see the new row; G3 queued, barrier unverified
rejection path unverified

faults.fault: pre-rename crash residue: tmp file stays in the target dir
faults.consequence: inert for indexing (the .tmp extension fails the media-extension gate, so no partial file is ever indexed; watcher picks the file only after the rename) but never cleaned - no cleanup path exists (verified). REQ-10: sweep stale tmp files at startup/scan so the upload either lands or not, with no residue

faults.fault: crash between placement and row write
faults.consequence: converges: the file is indexed by the next rescan (fs-wins)

events.notes: Synchronous row write; no intake involved. Placement verified: tmp named {filename}-{uuid}.tmp inside the target dir, mtime set pre-rename (feeds the snapshot identity), atomic rename (post_upload.rs). See G3 in utils/quint/pipeline/goals.json for the barrier.

events.name: API_DELETE
events.description: A client deletes an asset over HTTP: file and sidecar removed, row deleted.
effects: File removed, then sidecar, then thumbnail only when no other asset shares the content hash, then rows deleted; delete of an already-gone asset is idempotent.

faults.fault: crash between per-asset steps (file deleted, sidecar not; or rows still present)
faults.consequence: converges under FS-as-truth: file deletion precedes sidecar deletion, so the REQ-1 skip hole is not triggered; missing thumb heals via forced reprocess

sidecar alone is never indexed; residue is inert bytes. REQ-9: restart/scan logs orphan .xmp and never deletes it; logging must not act concurrently with in-flight mutations - see API_ASSIGN_ALBUM_DIR_MOVE for the cleanup-vs-assign overlap hazard
same per-asset windows repeat; dir-level cleanup (empty dir removal) unverified

events.notes: Watcher Remove echo afterwards is a no-op.

events.name: API_ASSIGN_ALBUM_DIR_MOVE
events.description: A client moves an album directory over HTTP: files on disk move and rows are updated in place, preserving asset identity.
effects: Files moved and rows updated in place, assetId preserved; a watcher echo is idempotent (ASS-1).

faults.consequence: no generation bump (verified); absorbed by open-fail/skip - unproven
transient at most, unproven

faults.fault: orphan-sidecar cleanup overlaps a copy-sidecar-first assign in flight
faults.consequence: cleanup deletes the destination sidecar copy between the copy and the media move; the media then lands without its sidecar - permanent metadata divergence. REQ-9 is log-only: orphan detection must not act concurrently with an in-flight assign; observation of the transient is safe and expected

events.notes: Subtree equals one ApiMove per descendant; a watcher echo is idempotent. See ASS-1.

events.name: API_READ_COMPRESSED
events.description: A client requests the compressed (thumbnail-sized) rendition of an asset over HTTP. Read-only; recorded to pin the observable serving guarantees.
effects: Complete bytes only - no torn or partial response (REQ-13); no state change.

faults.fault: thumbnail bytes missing though row exists
faults.consequence: currently served as 500, not 404 (verified); contract gap needs a home
prevented by atomic thumbnail write (REQ-13)

events.notes: Compressed read; read-only, no state change. See REQ-13.

events.name: API_READ_ORIGINAL
events.description: A client requests the original image bytes of an asset over HTTP. Read-only; recorded to pin the observable serving guarantees.
effects: Complete bytes only; no state change.

faults.fault: row exists but original file gone
faults.consequence: same missing-path handling as API_READ_MISSING (handlers unverified)

events.notes: Original read; read-only, no state change.

events.name: API_READ_MISSING
events.description: A client requests bytes for an asset whose file on disk is gone (or whose row is absent). Reads queue no watcher remove; nothing is healed by the read itself.
preconditions: row exists, file absent (or row absent)
effects: Graceful outcome (not-found or placeholder), no state change, no 500, no torn bytes.

faults.fault: serving handlers unverified for the missing path
faults.consequence: current behavior unconfirmed; 500-vs-404 contract gap open

events.notes: Row exists but file gone (or row absent); no watcher remove queued. Serving handler must degrade gracefully (not-found/placeholder), no state change, no 500, no torn bytes. Serving handlers unverified for the missing path.

events.name: API_READ_MOVED
events.description: A client requests bytes via the old path after the file was moved underneath (pre-subtree-model state, e.g. an out-of-band rename).
effects: Read via the old path behaves as missing; healed by scan; no state change on read.

faults.fault: heals only via the next scan
faults.consequence: same missing-path serving question as API_READ_MISSING

events.notes: Row under old path, file under new path (pre-subtree-model): observed via old path as missing; healed by scan. No state change on read.

events.name: WATCHER_GAP
events.description: Filesystem notifications stop arriving for a stretch - queue overflow, unsupported platform, watcher starting late, watcher disabled. Not tied to a single file; affects a set of paths at once. This is the event the rescan backstop exists for; naming it makes 'who notices' a first-class question.
preconditions: watcher notifications missing or stopped for a stretch
effects: Agreed: all changes during the gap are repaired by the next scan or sweep; nothing outside the gap window survives stale.

faults.consequence: a gap with no rescan and no backstop heals never (REQ-5, REQ-6 open)

events.notes: Modeled recovery: ScanRoot over the affected root queues present files and marks the root's sweep; ScanRoot plus SweepRoot repairs changes that occurred during the gap. The gap itself is the absence of events. The fairness owner is decided: Flag::Rescan while the watcher is enabled plus the user-enabled periodic backstop (ASS-7); REQ-5 and REQ-6 track the implementation. DB_LOSS recovery makes the rescan a defined recovery path, not just an optimization backstop.

events.name: PROCESS_CRASH
events.description: The backend dies mid-pipeline (mid-apply, mid-write). On restart, the state is whatever was durably written (redb flushes, completed file writes).
effects: Agreed: on restart the index converges again from filesystem plus recovery state; no torn rows are served.

faults.fault: crash between row write and derived write
faults.consequence: row claims an artifact that does not exist; heals on next rescan via missing-thumb forced reprocess

REQUIRED (agreed): sidecar and albuminfo writes must be atomic - implemented, gate pending (REQ-13) (temp+rename verified in sidecar_edit.rs:write_bytes_atomically, covering per-asset .xmp AND album .albuminfo.xmp; xmp_write.rs:write_sidecar_content)
converges on re-scan under FS-as-truth (ASS-3); recovery asserted, not yet proven

faults.fault: assign_album mid-crash separates asset from sidecar
faults.consequence: ADOPTED: copy the sidecar to the destination first (atomic write), then move the asset, then delete the old sidecar; crash windows leave only orphan sidecar copies (logged per REQ-9), never separated metadata. Cleanup must not race an in-flight assign - see API_ASSIGN_ALBUM_DIR_MOVE

events.notes: Modeled as ProcessCrash: volatile intake is lost, durable state kept (SCOPE-6). Restart plus scan converges from every interrupted state the model represents; partial durable writes are abstracted away by SCOPE-6. Atomic sidecar/albuminfo writes are implemented (temp+rename) and tracked as REQ-13 (gate pending). Crash-survey synthesis: every mutating operator orders filesystem-first, DB-last (edit_*, delete, upload tmp+rename), so interrupted states converge under FS-as-truth; rotate_image still writes the thumbnail first (REQ-11: adopted order sidecar -> thumbnail -> DB). assign_album still renames the asset first and then the sidecar with errors ignored (REQ-12: adopted order copy the sidecar first, move the asset, delete the old sidecar). Orphan residue is logged rather than strived against. The design-doc mutation journal (docs/design.md) has no verified code counterpart - grep confirmed zero hits in backend/src.

events.name: DERIVED_STORE_LOSS
events.description: Derived bytes referenced by rows are lost - either wiped (cache clear, disk pressure) or silently corrupted on disk. The scan sees the first case (presence) but not the second (it never checks artifact content).
effects: Deleted thumbnails are restored by the next scan: a missing artifact forces reprocess.
Corrupted thumbnails are not restored by today's scan: it does not check artifact content.
Agreed: rows carry a thumbnail checksum; the scan regenerates and restores the thumbnail on mismatch (REQ-8 open).

faults.fault: window between artifact loss and the next scan
faults.consequence: artifact reads serve 500 (verified) until the scan restores it
untouched by today's scan; agreed mitigation is a per-row artifact checksum checked at scan (REQ-8 open) - also closes the interrupted-rotate stale-thumbnail window (API_ROTATE_IMAGE)
unverified whether reads regenerate or serve them as-is; a scan-passed checksum narrows the window but does not close it

events.notes: Modeled as LoseThumbs: a missing artifact forces reprocess and is restored by the next scan. Deleted thumbnails are restored as part of scan (missing artifact forces reprocess); corrupted thumbnails are not discovered - content is not checked during normal scan. A per-row checksum makes scans robust (regenerate on mismatch); REQ-8 tracks it.

events.name: DB_LOSS
events.description: The metadata database is lost while the filesystem remains intact: Picasu restarts and fully re-scans, restoring the index from the filesystem-as-truth baseline. The ultimate reindex-from-nothing test.
effects: Agreed: restart plus full re-scan rebuilds the index from the filesystem alone; fresh assetIds; content-keyed derived artifacts survive untouched.

faults.fault: restart + re-scan recovery unmodeled and untested
faults.consequence: restoration to the FS-as-truth baseline is asserted, not proven

faults.fault: asset identity churn (fresh assetIds after rebuild)
faults.consequence: accepted under the FS-as-truth baseline; persistent references to assetIds (e.g. bookmarked URLs) unverified

events.notes: Modeled as DbLoss: rows and generations are cleared and the nextAssetId restarts; a full ScanRoot rebuild restores the filesystem-as-truth baseline with fresh assetIds. Asset identity need not survive (accepted).

events.name: API_EDIT_METADATA
events.description: A client edits metadata (tag, description, flags, rating, share, album membership) for one asset or a batch over HTTP. Sidecars (.xmp per asset, .albuminfo.xmp per album) are rewritten atomically and then the DB payload is stored; a failed sidecar write rolls back already-written sidecars and stores nothing.
effects: Bytes first: each item's sidecar lands before the store transaction commits the payload.
A batch interrupted by crash applies partially; retrying the edit converges (fs-wins reprocess reads the newer sidecar).
Sidecar and DB never disagree in opposite directions: failure aborts before the store phase.

faults.fault: crash after sidecar write(s), before DB flush
faults.consequence: sidecar ahead of row; rescan's present-sidecar forced reprocess converges the row
the code comment itself warns files may end up disagreeing with the cache in the direction only a reindex can fix - no verified convergence guarantee beyond scan

events.notes: PROPOSED/TBD - new event discovered by the multi-file crash survey (edit_tag, edit_description, edit_flags, edit_rating, edit_album, edit_share all route through commit_metadata_edits). Order verified: sidecars first, payloads second (sidecar_edit.rs doc). No success-path sidecar deletion verified; if reverting edits deletes a sidecar, the missing sidecar identity (REQ-1) applies and prevents convergence.

events.name: API_ROTATE_IMAGE
events.description: A client rotates an asset over HTTP. Four artifacts are involved: the compressed rendition, the thumbnail, the XMP sidecar (rotation persisted there), and the DB records. Verified order: thumbnail regenerated first, then sidecar write (failure aborts leaving DB and sidecar on the previous rotation together), then record flush.
events.target: compressed bytes + thumbnail + sidecar + row of one asset
effects: Settled state (no crash): thumbnail, sidecar rotation, and DB records all reflect the new rotation.
ADOPTED reorder (implement pending): write the sidecar rotation first, then the thumbnail, then merge dimensions/rotation/thumbhash into the DB records last.

faults.fault: current order places thumbnail before sidecar (the one deviation from the codebase's fs-first pattern)
faults.consequence: ADOPTED FIX (REQ-11): reorder to sidecar -> thumbnail -> DB. After reorder any post-sidecar interruption leaves a present sidecar, which forces reprocess; the pipeline re-derives rotation from the sidecar (verified source of truth, apply_rotation shared by endpoint and pipeline) and regenerates the thumbnail - converges
with the adopted order the abort precedes any other artifact change: DB, thumbnail, and sidecar all stay on the previous rotation

faults.fault: route doc says the compressed JPEG is written back; no such write located
faults.consequence: rotation is sidecar-carried and applied at decode (verified); the doc comment appears stale - confirm or correct it with the rotate change (REQ-11)

events.notes: Rotation source of truth is the sidecar (rotate_image.rs comment); apply_rotation (misc.rs) is shared by the endpoint and the index pipeline so a reindex reproduces the displayed rotation. The per-row artifact checksum (REQ-8) additionally guards the thumbnail-mismatch window against interrupted rotates of the current implementation.
